messages.subject: [FLR-list] New packages for R 3.4
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,



A new set of FLR packages has been uploaded today on the flr-project.org repository, with binary versions available for Windows on R 3.4. Please install them from there by calling



install.packages(repos="http://flr-project.org/R")



or by sourcing the installation script that will take care of all non-FLR dependencies



source("http://flr-project.org/R/instFLR.R")



Among this set of packages, we are releasing for the first time packages containing C++ that can (only) run on 64 bit R in Windows, and that will eventually substitute those currently working only in 32 bit R in Windows.



The new package versions available are as follows:



FLCore 2.6.5

FLa4a 1.1.3

FLEDA 2.5.1

FLFishery 0.1.2

FLFleet 2.6.0

FLSAM 1.02

diags 2.2.1

ggplotFL 2.6.2

FLRDynState 2.5.1



- Packages for 32bit R only



FLash 2.5.8

FLAssess 2.6.1

FLBEIA 1.15.1

FLBRP 2.5.2

FLife 2.1.2

FLXSA 2.6.0



- Packages for 64bit R only



FLRP 0.0.2

FLasher 0.0.3



FLRP and FLasher will become the new FLBRP and FLash respectively, and although they are still considered beta, they can already do most of what the old pkgs do, and even a few more in the caser of FLasher. More information on FLasher will follow soon.



Note that we do not currently have packages available for OSX, as we do not have access to the necessary hardware. If you are working on any of the flavours of OSX supported by R,Mavericks and El Capitan, and would like to help us preparing packages for OSX, please contact us.



Please do not hesitate reporting any issue, or positive feedback, either in the list or in the respective package issue page, for example https://github.com/flr/FLCore/issues



Best regards,





Iago, on behalf of the FLR Team

messages.subject: [FLR-list] current issues with package update - windows
messages.subject_clean: [FLR-list] current issues with package update - windows
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I just want to highlight an issue that seems to have popped up this week, that is creating issues with packages download and update in R Windows - nothing specific to FLR but generic to R.

I have downloaded and installed R3.4.1 this week - while at the same time it seems that Windows has proceeded with a big chunk of updates, my machine was busy with that yesterday. As a result, packages cannot be installed as usual; some packages and dependencies work fine, some others get blocked in temporary folders with the message "unable to move installation... ". They can only be used by downloading the binary zip from CRAN and unzip manually.
After a bit of time and help from our R experts, we believe that this may be linked to changes in the antivirus (Mc Afee), which blocks some packages. And according to R mailing list this is being looked at by R developers, and indeed today I could download and install packages by installing the R developer version patch 73329 and after... But since this would correspond to R3.5 then not all packages can yet be used with this devel version (ggplot2 crashes my R session).


So so.. well, I don't know if that is only me having this issue;-) But in case of this happens to others... you know

Bye

Clara

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I have seen this kind of problems in the past, specially with packages carrying a DLL or an executable file. Right now our web filter at the JRC sometimes blocks some FLR packages the first time it is downloaded.

If you cannot whitelist a website in your antivirus maybe you could create a local copy of CRAN inside your network, or one only wit the pkgs you need, for the time being.

Cheers,


Iago

Beth

Hi,



I  have been having this problem with installing R packages lately. I found a solution online that works for me.



https://stackoverflow.com/questions/5700505/windows-7-update-packages-problem-unable-to-move-temporary-installation<https://na01.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fstackoverflow.com%2Fquestions%2F5700505%2Fwindows-7-update-packages-problem-unable-to-move-temporary-installation&data=02%7C01%7Cebabcock%40rsmas.miami.edu%7Caf4be7c97a004227ecf108d503e3d126%7C2a144b72f23942d48c0e6f0f17c48e33%7C0%7C0%7C636419199377861115&sdata=8BEhjYy3yjmnY2j4PakxpcOuWcrwr2f1nENpsJx7vOo%3D&reserved=0>



Basically, you install the package in debug mode so that McAfee has time to scan all the files.



Beth

From: flr-list-bounces at lists.r-forge.r-project.org<mailto:flr-list-bounces at lists.r-forge.r-project.org> <flr-list-bounces at lists.r-forge.r-project.org<mailto:flr-list-bounces at lists.r-forge.r-project.org>> on behalf of Clara Ulrich <clu at aqua.dtu.dk<mailto:clu at aqua.dtu.dk>>
Sent: Friday, September 22, 2017 5:26 AM
To: flr-list at flr-project.org<mailto:flr-list at flr-project.org>
Subject: [FLR-list] current issues with package update - windows



Hi all,



I just want to highlight an issue that seems to have popped up this week, that is creating issues with packages download and update in R Windows ? nothing specific to FLR but generic to R.



I have downloaded and installed R3.4.1 this week ? while at the same time it seems that Windows has proceeded with a big chunk of updates, my machine was busy with that yesterday. As a result, packages cannot be installed as usual; some packages and dependencies work fine, some others get blocked in temporary folders with the message ?unable to move installation? ?. They can only be used by downloading the binary zip from CRAN and unzip manually.

After a bit of time and help from our R experts, we believe that this may be linked to changes in the antivirus (Mc Afee), which blocks some packages. And according to R mailing list this is being looked at by R developers, and indeed today I could download and install packages by installing the R developer version patch 73329 and after? But since this would correspond to R3.5 then not all packages can yet be used with this devel version (ggplot2 crashes my R session).





So so.. well, I don?t know if that is only me having this issue;-) But in case of this happens to others? you know



Bye



Clara

messages.subject: [FLR-list] FLR references
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,



As part of the new FLR website we have a a list of FLR-related publications at



http://www.flr-project.org/#publications



Right now it consists purely of peer review literature citing Kell et al. 2007.



I would like to extend it to have all papers, reports, grey, red and blue literature using FLR.



The source for the website is a BibteX file, kept at



https://github.com/flr/flr.github.io/blob/master/flr.bib



I would be most grateful if you could send me any reference not already in there for any peer-review paper, working document, working group report, or research project report in which FLR has been used or cited. A BibTex formatted reference would be ideal, but otherwise please send me a table (plain text, CSV or Excel) with at least



- Author(s)/Working Group/Research project name

- Title

- Year

- URL for PDF file, if possible



Please feel free to resend to anybody you suspect or know to have used FLR in the past



Thanks so much,





Iago
